clue.text: "Round of Golf here": item in Kent College prospectus

definitions.meaning: Royal St George's at Sandwich in Kent is a famous championship golf links, so a round is played on that course
a course of study that alternates college terms with periods in work, as a college prospectus would list

explanation.surface: A golfing round and a college brochure, both set in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent with a famous golf course; the second sense is a British term for a degree that includes a year in industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the golf links at the Kent town, and a study scheme sandwiching work placements between terms.

clue.text: Guards on the Underground?

parts.note: underground here means covert rather than the London tube, so these are guards working in secret

explanation.surface: Station staff patrolling the London tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The Underground is London's metro, but 'underground' also means clandestine.
explanation.definitionFit: A covert state force that watches citizens is a hidden guard, operating underground in the clandestine sense.

clue.text: Just the job for the corner-man!

definitions.text: Just the job for the corner-man!

parts.words: Just the job for the corner-man!
parts.note: a perfect fit of a role is a recess in a wall, the kind of spot found in a corner

explanation.surface: Ideal work for a boxer's cornerman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a suitable position in life and a recess set into a wall or corner.

clue.text: Stylish cover for a laptop!

parts.note: laptop read as the top of the lap, the waist area, which a smart garment covers

explanation.surface: A fashionable case for a portable computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart sleeveless garment covers the body just above the lap, a 'lap top' in a punning sense.

clue.text: A Frenchman's charge for electricity

parts.note: a French physicist gave his name to the unit of electric charge, not a bill for power

explanation.surface: A French householder's electricity bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electric charge is named after the French physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.

clue.text: One finds why people are late

definitions.text: One finds why people are late

parts.words: One finds why people are late
parts.note: late in the sense of deceased: this official establishes the cause of a death

explanation.surface: Someone investigating unpunctuality.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who holds inquests determines the cause of death of the late, meaning dead, people.

clue.text: Yours only houses a porcupine

indicators.note: the words Yours only contain, or house, the letters sought within them

explanation.surface: A claim that only your home holds a spiny rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the Canadian porcupine, a dictionary word beloved of setters.

clue.text: Weighing machine exposed crooked deal with tyres

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of deal with tyres are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A scales dealer caught in a dodgy tyre deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' and 'with' are links; 'crooked' rearranges DEAL and TYRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional balance with a sliding weight on a graduated arm is a type of weighing device.

clue.text: These growths have their points

parts.note: growths read as plants, and points as spines, rather than merits

explanation.surface: Tumours with some redeeming features.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert plants bristle with spines, so they literally have points.

clue.text: Rents due to be rendered without relief

indicators.note: rendered as in made over or turned into something else, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Rent payments due to be handed over, with no help available.
explanation.definitionFit: Without relief from fatigue means not having had any repose.

clue.text: The backbone of a porcupine?

parts.note: backbone in the usual sense, with the porcupine's quills suggesting a column of spines

explanation.surface: Asking about a spiny animal's spine.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone is the vertebral column, and a porcupine's quills make it a column of spines too.

clue.text: Opt for the return of gold plate

parts.note: to opt for something is to elect or choose it

indicators.note: the return of means the word for gold is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Choosing to get gold plate back.
explanation.definitionFit: This short form denotes electroplate, a metal coating deposited by electrolysis.

clue.text: In France no one in the field is able to stay fast

parts.note: the French word for no is non
a slip is a cricket fielder stationed beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: Nobody fielding in France can keep a grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket fielding position, near the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface or sole that grips stays fast, resisting sliding.

clue.text: Irish activist is out of condition

indicators.note: out of here means the word is is taken away from the condition word

parts.note: a proviso is a condition attached to an agreement

explanation.surface: An Irish campaigner looking unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IS from PROVISO leaves the informal name for a member of the Provisional IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for a member of the Provisional IRA, a militant Irish republican.

clue.text: Essential accompaniment moved Gobbi a lot

indicators.note: moved as in shifted around, so the letters of Gobbi a lot change places

explanation.surface: An operatic accompaniment that greatly stirred the baritone Tito Gobbi.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this term marks an accompanying part that must not be left out, an indispensable accompaniment.

clue.text: Silly fellow poked bard in rib

indicators.note: poked as in jabbed and jumbled, so the letters of bard in rib are stirred up

explanation.surface: A fool jabbed a poet in the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a stupid person, someone with a brain the size of a bird's.

clue.text: Cow, perhaps, a pest on the lawn

definitions.meaning: a traditional pet name for a dairy cow
a yellow-flowered weed that spreads across grass

explanation.surface: A cow is described as a nuisance on the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stock name for a cow and also a common yellow weed of lawns.

clue.text: Blend basil into alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: blend as in mix together, so the letters of basil and into are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe mixing basil into spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: These are drinks, especially alcoholic ones, often poured out as offerings.

clue.text: Sinister contents of room in 'ouse of 'orrors

indicators.note: contents of points to letters held inside the words room in 'ouse

explanation.surface: Something creepy inside a chamber in a house of horrors, in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped aitches ('ouse, 'orrors) are a Cockney accent; 'of 'orrors' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister and threatening are near synonyms, both suggesting something bad is coming.

clue.text: One who gets the taste for embroidery

definitions.meaning: someone who tries a little of something to judge it
a piece of needlework showing a range of stitches

explanation.surface: A taster who takes up needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a person who tries things out and a decorative stitched piece showing varied stitches.

clue.text: Like a bore, the boy brings it back

indicators.note: brings, with back, says the boy and it are carried the other way round
back completes the signal that the letters run in the reverse direction

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster brings a dull person home.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore here is a tidal wave surging up a river, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A river bore is a surge caused by the incoming tide, so it is of the tide.

clue.text: Mountains of wine in Tuscany

definitions.meaning: a range of hills in Tuscany
a red wine produced in that Tuscan district

explanation.surface: A great quantity of Tuscan wine.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the hilly district between Florence and Siena and its famous red wine.

clue.text: Bare, with no arms

definitions.meaning: unarmed, as in a ... blade or defenceless person

explanation.surface: Unclothed and unarmed.
explanation.definitionFit: It means unclothed, and also defenceless or without weapons, as in naked to one's enemies.

clue.text: The conductor's card

definitions.meaning: a distinguished musician who leads an orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader's calling card.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an honorific for a great conductor and the name of a well-known debit card brand.

clue.text: Rat is gnawing bones

indicators.note: gnawing chews things up, so the letters of rat is are chewed into another order

explanation.surface: A rodent chewing on bones.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the bones of the ankle or of an insect's foot.

clue.text: Save bread! An angel will do it

parts.note: to bank money is to save it
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A plea to preserve loaves, with a heavenly helper on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: An angel is theatre slang for a financial backer, not a heavenly being.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer of a show, an angel, funds it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Good Lord! Few spoke here

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like good lord

indicators.note: spoke tells us the word few is said out loud rather than spelt

parts.note: few spoken gives the final sound

explanation.surface: An exclamation that hardly anyone spoke here.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a Cockney exclamation; 'here' is the place, the Greek island the exclamation sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island is the place meant, the answer to where this sentence refers.

clue.text: Picture of Patience in file of recruits

indicators.note: of links the picture to Patience, giving the possessive order with the patient man first

parts.note: the biblical Job is the proverbial model of patience
a description paints a picture in words

explanation.surface: A portrait of patience kept in a recruitment folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The patience of Job' is proverbial, so Job stands for Patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel files of new recruits hold a written account of their duties, which is what this phrase names.
